chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If it is a 'ajmah (a body of water or a net/enclosure) in which there is no reed (or grass), something of the fish is taken out and sold, and what is in the 'ajmah."

key_terms.أَجَمَة: A body of water or an enclosure/net, often referring to a specific type of fishery or water body.
key_terms.السَّمَكِ: The fish, the subject of the commercial transaction.
key_terms.قَصَب: Reed or grass, used here to describe the vegetation or lack thereof in the water body.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on selling fish from a body of water without reeds?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the permissibility of selling fish from an 'ajmah' (a net or enclosed water body) when it lacks reeds, thereby removing the element of *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the quantity or quality of the catch. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing speculative risk in commercial transactions by ensuring the commodity is accessible and identifiable before sale.
